items.task: Take one old, non-confidential precedent agreement and strip every party name, date and figure by hand. Save it as your practice document.
items.why: You cannot practise on client material, so make a safe copy first.

items.task: Ask the assistant for a one-paragraph summary of the practice document. Then read the summary against the document and mark every sentence true or false.
items.why: Your first summary invented a clause; this time you check it.

items.task: Ask for the summary again but tell the model to quote the clause number for every statement. Check each quote exists.
items.skill: verify a claim against the source
items.why: Forcing citations makes invented clauses easy to catch.

items.task: Ask the assistant to list every defined term in the practice document as a two-column table: term, clause where defined.
items.why: Tables are easier to check than prose.

items.task: Write down, in one paragraph, the three things you always look for in a supply agreement redline. Save it as your standard position note.
items.why: The model needs your standard position in writing before it can compare against it.

items.task: Give the model your standard position note and the practice document. Ask which of the three points the document meets and which clause proves it.
items.skill: verify a claim against the source
items.why: A first small version of the deviation review.

items.task: Ask the assistant to draft a three-sentence client email explaining one clause in plain language. Edit it until you would send it.
items.why: Drafting to edit rather than from scratch is the habit you want.

items.task: Make a second copy of the practice document and change five clauses by hand. Ask the model to list the differences between the two copies.
items.why: This is the redline comparison, on material you control.

items.task: Check the model's difference list against your five changes. Note what it missed and what it invented.
items.why: Knowing the failure modes is what makes the tool usable.

items.task: Ask for the difference list again as a table: clause, our wording, their wording, significance (high, medium, low). Check the significance column.
items.why: The deviation table is the artefact you want at the end.

items.task: Write a reusable prompt that produces the deviation table from any two documents. Save it in your notes.
items.why: A saved prompt turns a good result into a repeatable one.

items.task: Ask the model to explain one clause of the practice document to a non-lawyer in five sentences. Check every sentence against the clause.
items.why: Plain-language explanation is most of an advice note.

items.task: Redact a real, closed matter's agreement using find and replace for names, dates and figures. Check it twice before it leaves your machine.
items.why: A real document, made safe, gives realistic practice.

items.task: Run your saved deviation prompt on the redacted real agreement against your standard position note. Check every row.
items.skill: verify a claim against the source
items.why: First real run of the workflow, on safe material.

items.task: Ask the assistant to draft a short advice note from the checked deviation table. Edit it to your standard.
items.why: Table in, note out: the second half of your goal.

items.task: Time yourself: redact, run the deviation prompt, check, draft the note. Write down how long each step took.
items.why: You cannot improve the hour without measuring it.

items.task: Ask the model to list the questions it would need answered before it could assess a clause it flagged. Answer them yourself.
items.why: Good questions from the model show where it is guessing.

items.task: Ask for a fee estimate structure for a redline review as an Excel-ready table: task, hours, rate. Adjust the hours to reality.
items.why: Estimates are structured extraction too.

items.task: Take a scanned PDF from a closed matter, redact it, and ask the assistant to transcribe one page. Compare against the scan.
items.skill: verify a claim against the source
items.why: Scans are where transcription errors hide.

items.task: Ask the model to translate one redacted clause from Chinese to English and back. Note what changed in meaning.
items.why: Round-trip translation exposes drift.

items.task: Give the model two versions of your own standard position note and ask which is clearer and why. Pick one.
items.why: Your own writing benefits from the same comparison.

items.task: Write a prompt that drafts an advice note from a deviation table in your house style. Include two example paragraphs of your real writing (redacted).
items.why: Examples of your voice beat descriptions of it.

items.task: Run the full workflow on a second redacted closed matter. Time it again and compare with day 16.
items.why: Second measurement shows whether the saved prompts help.

items.task: Ask the assistant to find every clause in the redacted agreement that references another clause, and check the references resolve.
items.skill: verify a claim against the source
items.why: Cross-reference checking is tedious for people and cheap for models.

items.task: Draft a one-page internal note on how you now review redlines with AI, including what you never paste in. Edit until a colleague could follow it.
items.why: Writing the process down protects confidentiality and spreads the skill.

items.task: Ask the model to critique your internal note as a sceptical senior partner would. Address two of its points.
items.why: Adversarial review is one of the best uses of the tool.

items.task: Build a checklist of the model's failure modes you have seen this month: invented clauses, missed changes, wrong significance. Keep it next to your prompts.
items.why: A failure checklist is your quality control.

items.task: Run the deviation prompt with the checklist appended, telling the model to flag anything it is unsure about. See whether the flags are useful.
items.why: Asking for uncertainty gets you fewer confident errors.

items.task: On a redacted matter, produce the deviation table and advice note end to end, checking each row against the source before drafting.
items.skill: verify a claim against the source
items.why: Dress rehearsal for the real thing.

items.task: Write a short review: what the workflow now takes in minutes, which steps still need your judgement, and what you will try next month.
items.why: Reflection turns 30 days of tasks into a habit.
